units.passage: You ask ChatGPT, “How do you swap two variables in C?”, read the answer, and close the window.
units.why: Asking a syntax question, reading the answer and closing the window is listed as consulting; closing before writing fits P23 (keep AI apart from the work).
units.fit_note: Example of acceptable consulting; includes asking a syntax question as well as closing the window. / Also illustrates closing the window afterward (P23); first listed instance of the question.

units.passage: It is okay to use AI to brainstorm ideas or to scrutinize your argument but never, ever, copy-paste AI text into your writing.
units.why: 'never, ever, copy-paste AI text into your writing' bans copy-pasting from AI, P23.
units.fit_note: Also a ban on AI-generated text in the student's writing (P19).

units.passage: Beyond bibliographies, you are not allowed to copy and paste material generated by AI and use it in your assignments.
units.policy: you are not allowed to copy and paste material generated by AI and use it in your assignments
units.why: "you are not allowed to copy and paste material generated by AI and use it in your assignments" is a copy-paste ban; P23 names 'never copy-paste from it' directly, so P23 rather than P19 (which is about having AI produce the work).

units.passage: I affirm I did not generate text with artificial intelligence and directly copy it into my paper.
units.policy: I affirm I did not generate text with artificial intelligence and directly copy it into my paper.
units.why: "I affirm I did not generate text with artificial intelligence and directly copy it into my paper" is an affirmation that AI text is not copied into the paper; this is the copy-paste rule (P23), not P19.

units.passage: You remain responsible for all content you submit for evaluation and should not simply cut and paste large chunks of GAI outputs into your work.
units.why: Student "should not simply cut and paste large chunks of GAI outputs into your work" limits copying under permission; closest is P23 (never copy-paste from it) though it is soft, should-not.

units.passage: I recommend that you do not have your assignment and the GAI tool open on your device at the same time.
units.why: "I recommend that you do not have your assignment and the GAI tool open on your device at the same time" keeps the AI and the work apart, so P23.

units.passage: Instead, take notes in your own words while you interact with the GAI tool, then use your notes to remind you of what you’ve learned and to inform your work.
units.why: "take notes in your own words while you interact with the GAI tool, then use your notes" is a way of working that keeps AI chat apart from the work, so P23.
units.fit_note: The note-taking in own words is how one may use AI while keeping the work separate.

units.passage: Never copy output from GAI tools into your assignment.
units.why: "Never copy output from GAI tools into your assignment" is a plain ban on copy-paste from AI, so P23.

units.passage: then close the interaction down, open your assignment, and let your assignment reflect your improved understanding.
units.why: Students should 'close the interaction down, open your assignment, and let your assignment reflect your improved understanding', keeping AI use and writing apart (P23).

units.passage: It is wiser and safer to adapt the principles demonstrated in those snippets to your own code,
units.policy: It is wiser and safer to adapt the principles demonstrated in those snippets to your own code, and to the context in which the snippets need to run, rather than simply pasting something into your code verbatim.
units.why: 'It is wiser and safer to adapt the principles demonstrated in those snippets to your own code... rather than simply pasting something into your code verbatim' is advice against pasting; nearest is P23, which covers not copy-pasting from AI.
units.fit_note: Framed as a professional-safety recommendation, not a strict separation of AI and work.

units.passage: After the interaction, turn off any AI-based assistance and write your assignments independently to reflect your revised knowledge.
units.why: MECH 121: 'turn off any AI-based assistance and write your assignments independently'; keep AI apart from writing, P23.
units.fit_note: Pairs with permission to use AI beforehand as preparation.

units.passage: If you decide to use AI-generated text, you must type it manually into your composition.
units.why: 'If you decide to use AI-generated text, you must type it manually into your composition. Do not insert or cut and paste.' requires keeping AI output apart from the work. P23 fits because copy-paste is banned.
units.fit_note: Sample statement requiring manual retyping rather than a separate window.
